data.name: Abalone
data.detailed_description:
Descubra nossa nova versão com novíssimos gráficos inspirados na edição moderna do famoso jogo de estratégia. Há quase 30 anos, Abalone é considerado um dos melhores jogos disponíveis, conhecido pelo seu tabuleiro hexagonal e peças pretas e brancas. O objetivo desse jogo de estratégia abstrato é simples: empurrar as peças do seu oponente para fora do tabuleiro! Mas cuidado, não é fácil dominar o jogo, então fique esperto e mostre que está à altura do desafio!
TENHA UM PLANO DE ATAQUE... Crie um plano de ataque para empurrar as peças do seu oponente para fora do tabuleiro. A cada rodada, você pode andar um espaço em qualquer direção com 1, 2 ou 3 peças alinhadas. Quando você está numa posição de Sumito (isto é, quando suas bolinhas estão em número maior e em contato com as do oponente) é possível empurrar as peças dele pra fora! Por exemplo, você precisa de três peças pretas para empurrar uma ou duas peças brancas. Não adianta nada se apressar; é melhor ficar tranquilo e pensar em todas as possibilidades, já que um movimento precipitado pode te colocar numa posição ruim e fazer a vitória escapar de suas mãos.
...E DE DEFESA.
Se você quer vencer, a chave é não atacar, mas assumir posições específicas com certas combinações de movimentos. Assim como no xadrez e damas, pode-se tentar criar armadilhas sacrificando peças ou posições estratégicas para bloquear o oponente. Os pontos de contato mais perigosos são nas bordas do tabuleiro, onde um movimento ruim significa a perda de uma peça ou do jogo todo! Às vezes, é melhor desenvolver o seu lado zen e ser paciente se quiser vencer!
NÃO CONFUNDA PREVISÃO COM AFOBAÇÃO
A chave da vitória está em prever e analisar as jogadas do oponente. Apesar do jogo ser fácil de aprender, ele requer estratégia e raciocínio. Para aprimorar o seu pensamento estratégico, o jogo oferece vários modos que permitem revisar suas partidas jogada a jogada. Por exemplo, o Modo Desafio te ajuda a se tornar um verdadeiro mestre de Abalone, um movimento de cada vez. Os desafios vão ficando mais difíceis conforme você avança. Por exemplo, no começo é preciso empurrar só uma peça para vencer, e então duas, e o mestre do dojo vai ficando cada vez mais difícil.
JOGUE SOZINHO OU COM AMIGOS
Jogue sozinho contra o computador no Modo Desafio ou no Modo Partida Livre, ou contra seus amigos. No Modo Passe e Jogue, você pode duelar no mesmo dispositivo! Cansado de jogar com seus amigos? Encare os melhores jogadores do mundo no Modo Online acessando sua conta Asmodee!
Recursos:
  • Solo:
    - 3 níveis de dificuldade contra a IA (Fácil, Médio, Difícil)
    - Uma campanha solo com desafios únicos
    - Um modo de jogo que permite criar o seu próprio jogo, suas próprias regras e posicionar as primeiras peças
  • Multijogador:
    - Modo Passe e Jogue
    - Modo Online
  • Disponível em inglês, francês, alemão, espanhol, italiano, português e holandês.

reviews.review:
Abalone is a digital adaptation of the classic abstract strategy board game that combines straightforward mechanics with surprisingly intricate tactical possibilities. Developed and published under the Games-Up label, the game challenges players to outmaneuver their opponents on a hexagonal board by strategically positioning marbles and pushing opposing pieces beyond its boundaries. Its emphasis on logical thinking, positional awareness, and calculated decision-making makes it an appealing experience for enthusiasts of traditional tabletop strategy games. Rather than relying on elaborate visuals or complicated mechanics, it demonstrates how a simple concept can generate meaningful strategic depth.

The gameplay revolves around controlling black or white marbles arranged across a hexagonal playing field. Players alternate turns, moving individual marbles or groups of up to three aligned pieces in different directions. The primary objective is to push six opposing marbles off the board before losing six of your own. Central to this system is the Sumito mechanic, which allows stronger formations to push smaller opposing groups when the appropriate conditions are satisfied. Understanding how to exploit numerical advantages while maintaining defensive stability is essential to achieving victory.

What makes the experience particularly engaging is the constant balance between offensive pressure and defensive positioning. Aggressive movements can create opportunities to eliminate opposing pieces, but poorly planned attacks may leave important formations vulnerable. Maintaining control of central positions, protecting exposed marbles, and anticipating an opponent's next move become increasingly important as matches progress. Every decision carries consequences, encouraging players to think several turns ahead rather than focusing exclusively on immediate gains.

The single-player component offers three difficulty settings, allowing newcomers to familiarize themselves with the rules before confronting more demanding computer-controlled opponents. Easy difficulty provides an approachable environment for learning movement patterns and basic tactics, while Medium and Hard introduce greater strategic challenges. This adjustable structure makes the game accessible to different skill levels, although experienced players may eventually find that the computer opposition cannot fully replicate the unpredictability and creativity of human competitors.

Challenge Mode adds another layer of engagement by presenting structured scenarios that test specific strategic abilities. Players must complete objectives involving marble movement, positional manipulation, and carefully executed pushing combinations. These challenges serve as useful exercises for understanding the underlying mechanics while providing an alternative to conventional matches. Their gradually increasing complexity encourages experimentation and helps players recognize tactical opportunities that might otherwise remain unnoticed.

Free Play Mode expands the available options by allowing players to customize matches and experiment with different starting arrangements. This flexibility is particularly valuable for individuals interested in exploring unconventional strategies or recreating specific board situations. The ability to establish personalized scenarios adds replay value, while move-review functionality provides opportunities to examine previous decisions and identify potential improvements.

Multiplayer is another important attraction. Pass & Play functionality allows two people to compete on the same computer, preserving much of the competitive atmosphere associated with the physical board game. Online multiplayer is also advertised through an Asmodee account, although the continued reliability and availability of its online services should not be assumed. Local competition remains especially appealing because human opponents introduce unpredictable tactics and creative approaches that can make repeated matches considerably more interesting.

Visually, Abalone embraces a clean and minimalist presentation that closely resembles its tabletop counterpart. The contrasting marbles and recognizable hexagonal board create an environment where players can concentrate on strategy without unnecessary distractions. Although the graphics lack the sophistication of contemporary high-budget games, their simplicity complements the experience. The straightforward interface and uncomplicated visual design make the essential information easy to understand, even during increasingly complex tactical situations.

Accessibility is another advantage, particularly because the rules are relatively easy to learn despite their strategic depth. The game also supports multiple interface languages, broadening its appeal among international audiences. Its modest storage requirements make it a lightweight addition to a PC library. However, players seeking extensive progression systems, narrative content, elaborate customization, or substantial gameplay variety may find the experience limited. Most of its longevity comes from mastering the same fundamental mechanics rather than discovering entirely new features.

The game's greatest weakness is its relatively narrow focus. Although the available modes provide different ways to engage with the board, the underlying experience remains largely unchanged. Matches can become repetitive for players who do not particularly enjoy abstract strategy games. Furthermore, the quality of the digital adaptation depends on factors such as control responsiveness, artificial intelligence, and multiplayer stability, which cannot be fully established through the store description alone.

Steam Deck compatibility remains officially unconfirmed, with no verified compatibility classification established from the available information. Its lightweight graphics and turn-based mechanics suggest that handheld play could be practical, but potential issues involving Proton, touchscreen interaction, controller mapping, and interface scaling remain uncertain. Consequently, it should be considered a game with unknown Steam Deck compatibility rather than one guaranteed to function properly.

Overall, Abalone succeeds conceptually by translating an established board game into an accessible digital strategy experience. Its satisfying positional mechanics, customizable matches, structured challenges, and multiplayer options provide worthwhile entertainment for players who enjoy thoughtful competition. While its limited variety and uncertain technical compatibility prevent it from appealing universally, its strategic foundation remains compelling. For enthusiasts of chess-like tactical encounters and traditional abstract board games, it offers an enjoyable opportunity to test patience, foresight, and decision-making.

A rewarding abstract strategy experience featuring accessible rules, meaningful tactical depth, and flexible gameplay modes, although limited variety and uncertain online functionality slightly diminish its overall appeal.

Rating: 7/10
